title: The Enchiridion
author: Epictetus
translator: Thomas Wentworth Higginson (public domain, Project Gutenberg #45109)
blurb: A pocket handbook from a philosopher born a slave: separate what you control from what you don't, and you will never be a slave again.

impediment.m: Something that blocks or slows you.
impediment.e: His injury was an impediment to playing football.

banquet.e: The wedding banquet had twenty dishes.

drama.m: A play; a story acted out.
drama.e: The school drama needed someone to play the king.

cards.title: Control what you can
cards.text: The whole handbook rests on one split. Some things are up to us: our opinions, aims, desires and dislikes. Others are not: our body, property, reputation and position. Treat the second kind as yours and you will be frustrated and blame everyone. Focus on the first and nobody can harm you.
cards.quote: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
cards.qMean: Some things you can control; some things you can't.
cards.qLife: You can't control the traffic, but you can control when you leave home.

cards.title: It's the story you tell
cards.text: We are not upset by events, but by our judgements about them. Death is not terrible — otherwise Socrates would have feared it. When we are troubled, we should blame our own views, not others.
cards.quote: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
cards.qMean: What upsets us is not what happens, but what we think about it.
cards.qLife: Two people stuck in the same rain: one is miserable, the other enjoys the smell.
cards.cap: David - The Death of Socrates · public domain

cards.title: Wish for what is
cards.text: Don't demand that the world go your way. Wish instead that things happen as they actually do happen, and you will live at peace.
cards.quote: Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
cards.qMean: Stop insisting things go your way; accept how they go, and life is easier.
cards.qLife: Rain on your picnic day? Move it indoors and have fun anyway.
cards.cap: Wheel of Fortune with the Fates · public domain

cards.title: The body can be stopped
cards.text: Illness can stop the body, but not the will — unless the will agrees. Lameness stops the leg, not the mind. Whatever happens, ask what it stops, and you'll find it stops something else, not you.
cards.quote: Sickness is an impediment to the body, but not to the will unless itself pleases.
cards.qMean: Illness can limit your body, but not your choices, unless you let it.
cards.qLife: A friend with a broken leg who still finishes her course online.
cards.cap: Marble statue of a draped seated man · public domain

cards.title: Nothing is lost, only returned
cards.text: Never say 'I have lost it' — say 'I have given it back.' Everything we have is on loan from life. While it is with you, take care of it, as a traveller takes care of an inn.
cards.quote: Never say of anything, “I have lost it,” but, “I have restored it.”
cards.qMean: Don't call things lost; think of them as returned to where they came from.
cards.qLife: When an old phone dies, being grateful for the years it worked.
cards.cap: Roman funeral relief, Galleria Borghese · public domain

cards.title: Take a modest share
cards.text: Behave in life as at a dinner party. When a dish comes to you, take a polite portion. If it passes you by, don't grab at it. If it hasn't come yet, wait. Treat children, money and status the same way.
cards.quote: Remember that you must behave as at a banquet.
cards.qMean: Act in life like a polite guest at a big dinner.
cards.qLife: Not pushing for a promotion that isn't open yet, but being ready when it comes.
cards.cap: Banquet scene, fresco from Herculaneum · public domain

cards.title: Play your role well
cards.text: You are an actor in a play written by someone else. Whether your part is short or long, poor or royal, your job is to play it well; choosing the part is not.
cards.quote: Remember that you are an actor in a drama of such sort as the Author chooses
cards.qMean: You don't choose your role in life, but you choose how well you play it.
cards.qLife: Being the best possible assistant manager instead of sulking about not being the boss.
cards.cap: Theatre masks, Roman mosaic, Naples · public domain

cards.title: They think they're right
cards.text: When someone harms or insults you, remember they acted on what seemed right to them. If they are wrong, they are the ones deceived and hurt. Say to yourself: 'It seemed so to him.'
cards.quote: When any person does ill by you, or speaks ill of you, remember that he acts or speaks from an impression that it is right for him to do so.
cards.qMean: When someone hurts you, remember they believe they're right.
cards.qLife: The driver who honked at you probably thought you cut him off.
cards.cap: The Orator (Aulus Metellus), Roman bronze · public domain
